$comment: Single source of truth for the Attachment API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: attachment
title: Attachment
description: A file or picture attached to a message: an icon or thumbnail, the name, its size and type, and an optional remove button. Shows upload progress and failed uploads too.
thumb: design-brief.pdfPDF · 2.4 MB

name.description: The file name. Also the picture's alt text and part of each button's label.

type / size.description: Shown as "PDF · 2.4 MB" (size is in bytes; formatBytes does the rounding).

meta.description: Your own line under the name instead of type and size.

thumbnail.description: A picture: replaces the icon in a file row, or fills the tile.

icon.description: Your own icon instead of the file icon.

href / download.description: Makes it a link, for files already sent.

progress.description: 0–100 while uploading: shows "Uploading… 64%" and a small progress bar.

error.description: The upload failed: the message replaces the size.

onRemove / onRetry.description: Show a remove (or cancel) button, and a retry button after an error.

AttachmentList.description: A wrapping row of attachments, e.g. above the message box. label names the list.

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Files waiting to be sent: a document, one with a thumbnail and a picture tile, each with a remove button.

examples.title: Uploading and failed
examples.description: A progress bar while the file uploads, then an error with retry.

examples.title: In a sent message
examples.description: Once sent, attachments are links that open or download the file.

a11y: Attachments sit in a labelled list, so screen readers say how many files there are.
Every button names its file: "Remove design-brief.pdf", "Retry recording.mov".
Upload progress is a progressbar named after the file, with its value. The error is plain text next to the name, and is shown by an icon and a red edge, not colour alone.
A picture tile uses the file name as its alt text; thumbnails in a file row are decorative (alt="") because the name is right next to them.
